video.title: Alphabet To Raise $80B in Equity, Anthropic Files For IPO | Bloomberg Tech 6/2/2026
video.display_title_html: Alphabet To Raise $80B in Equity, Anthropic Files For IPO

thesis: A historic wave of AI-driven capital raising — Alphabet's $80B equity sale, and the SpaceX/Anthropic/OpenAI mega-IPO race — is testing whether public markets can absorb trillions in interdependent AI bets.

chapters.title: SpaceX Pushes Banks for Low IPO Fees
SpaceX IPO will Herald 'True Space Age': Impulse Space

insights.headline: Alphabet's $80B raise structured to limit dilution
insights.body: Alphabet's equity package splits into a $10B Berkshire Hathaway investment, $30B in public offerings, and a $40B at-the-market (ATM) program selling shares over time starting July 1st — one of the largest equity deals ever, funding AI CapEx.

insights.headline: Equity over debt signals extreme ROI confidence
insights.body: BI's Robert Shiffman notes weighted-average-cost-of-capital math says issue debt, yet Alphabet is raising equity — and getting Berkshire's backing — implying such confidence in AI investment returns that they want a massive 'kitty' regardless of cost.

insights.headline: Hyperscaler CapEx headed to $5 trillion over five years
insights.body: Shiffman estimates the biggest hyperscalers will spend ~$800B cumulatively this year, over $1 trillion next year, and $5 trillion over five years; Alphabet's own CapEx could hit $300B next year versus ~$190B now.

insights.headline: Anthropic files confidentially, beating OpenAI to IPO
insights.body: Anthropic submitted a draft S-1, pulling ahead of OpenAI, which is expected to file within weeks. Sam Altman said OpenAI will go public 'when it feels like it,' not before ready. Going first could set the narrative.

insights.headline: Anthropic at $47B annualized revenue run-rate
insights.body: Anthropic's run-rate revenue projection hit ~$47B, with the CEO citing an 80x increase in that projection in the first quarter year-over-year — extreme growth paired with still-high costs.

insights.headline: Mega-IPOs exceed a decade of VC listings
insights.body: PitchBook's Emily Jang: past 10 years of US VC-backed public listings total $1.5T; SpaceX alone ($75B) would exceed that decade figure, and OpenAI plus Anthropic target a combined ~$100B — more than all IPO proceeds raised in the past decade.

insights.headline: AI's circular dependency is the systemic risk
insights.body: Anthropic pays SpaceX ~$1.25B/month for compute while relying on Google/Amazon; 30% of US VC-backed startups are AI-native or adjacent. Interdependent cap tables and pricing mean one flop could cascade across the whole market.

insights.headline: SpaceX squeezing record-low bank underwriting fees
insights.body: SpaceX is negotiating below 0.75% on its $75B IPO — among the lowest ever. Split across 20+ banks that's ~$500M; Morgan Stanley and Goldman lead. Banks accept thin fees to attach their names to a historic deal and future pipeline.

insights.headline: Space tugs: the highways from low orbit outward
insights.body: Impulse Space's Tom Mueller (SpaceX employee #1) builds 'space tugs' that take over where launch ends. Its Helios vehicle — 'a rocket on a rocket' — reaches geosynchronous orbit in one day versus months for normal transfer orbits.

insights.headline: Perplexity's hybrid local-cloud inference orchestrator
insights.body: Aravind Srinivas describes a chip-agnostic OS-like layer that routes each AI workload between local device and cloud frontier models based on privacy, accuracy, intelligence, and cost — optimizing 'token value per watt per user' rather than centralizing all compute.

insights.headline: Perplexity optimizes retention, not engagement time
insights.body: Srinivas says accurate first-turn answers shorten sessions, so Perplexity measures repeat research uses instead. Subscription mix shifted from 9:91 to ~30:70 toward the $200/month Max plan — power users paying ~$2,000/year out of pocket.

insights.headline: HPE raises guidance, pulls 2028 outlook forward two years
insights.body: HPE stock surged ~21% to a record, adding ~$13B in market cap, on sales forecast up to 33% and EPS midpoint of $3.40 ($1 higher). Networking is now an $11B business; orders rose triple digits in servers, storage, and private cloud.

insights.headline: Memory needs shared risk, not just chipmakers
insights.body: ARM CEO Rene Haas argues asking public firms like Micron to bear all memory-capacity risk is unsustainable; expect novel models — hyperscalers investing in fabs, equity partnerships for secure supply — plus government support to smooth boom-bust cycles.

insights.headline: White House AI order: voluntary, classified model vetting
insights.body: Trump's AI executive order has the government work voluntarily with developers to access frontier models and assess cybersecurity risk, vetted by cleared experts in a top-secret process — released the same day Anthropic widened access to its 'mythos' model.

action_items: If you take one thing from this, watch the SpaceX June 11th IPO as the bellwether — its reception likely decides whether Anthropic and OpenAI list in 2026 or wait out the volatility.
Map AI exposure for circular dependency, not just direct bets: Anthropic pays SpaceX ~$1.25B/month and relies on Google/Amazon, so a single flop can ripple across interlinked cap tables.
For AI infrastructure, treat orchestration (local vs. cloud routing) as the cost lever — optimize token value per watt per user rather than running everything through frontier models.
